note: 豹貓, whose alternate name is 石虎 and which holds every leopard cat record. MDD v2.5 calls the species Mainland Leopard Cat, after the 2017 split from the Sunda Leopard Cat; Leopard Cat is the name the team uses. MDD's name stays searchable as an alternate. The subspecies 石虎 (P. b. euptilurus, t0105762) inherits this.

洋燕. TaiCOL keeps Hirundo tahitica whole; Clements v2025 split it, and gives the name Hirundo tahitica, and the name Tahiti Swallow, to a bird of the Society Islands. TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 洋燕 as Hirundo javanica, Pacific Swallow. The subspecies namiyei (49 records) inherits this.

棕耳鵯. TaiCOL gives this row the authority (Stresemann, 1912), which belongs to the Banggai golden bulbul Hypsipetes harterti, so the build took it for that species. The bird recorded in Taiwan is the brown-eared bulbul (TWBF 2026). Worth reporting to TaiCOL. The alternates that came with the wrong match (Banggai Golden-Bulbul) are dropped: that bird is not part of this taxon, so its name must not find this one in a search.

綠簑鷺. Clements v2025 split the species TaiCOL calls Butorides striata and keeps Striated Heron for B. striata in the narrow sense; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 綠簑鷺 as B. atricapilla, Little Heron. The subspecies carcinophila, actophila and amurensis inherit this.

叉尾雨燕. AviList's Apus pacificus has no Clements v2025 name, so the build fell back to AviList's own, Fork-tailed Swift; TWBF 2026, which follows Clements, lists Taiwan's 叉尾雨燕 as Pacific Swift. The subspecies pacificus and kurodae inherit this.
黃腹花蜜鳥. Clements v2025 calls Cinnyris jugularis in the narrow sense Garden Sunbird; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 黃腹花蜜鳥 as C. ornatus, Ornate Sunbird.
花翅山椒鳥. Clements v2025 calls Coracina macei in the narrow sense Indian Cuckooshrike; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 花翅山椒鳥 as C. javensis, Oriental Cuckooshrike.
星鴉. Clements v2025 calls Nucifraga caryocatactes in the narrow sense Northern Nutcracker; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 星鴉 as N. hemispila, Southern Nutcracker.

黃頭鷺. Clements v2025 calls what is left of the cattle egret after its split Western Cattle-Egret; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 黃頭鷺 as Ardea coromanda, Eastern Cattle-Egret. The subspecies coromandus already gets this name from the build.
白腹毛腳燕. Clements v2025 calls Delichon urbicum in the narrow sense Western House-Martin; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 白腹毛腳燕 as D. lagopodum, Siberian House-Martin.
黃腹鷚. Clements v2025 calls Anthus rubescens in the narrow sense American Pipit; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 黃腹鷚 as A. japonicus, Siberian Pipit.
白頭鶇. Clements v2025 split the island thrushes and gives Turdus poliocephalus in the narrow sense the name Tasman Sea Island-Thrush; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 白頭鶇 as T. niveiceps, Taiwan Thrush.
白燕鷗. Clements v2025 calls Gygis alba in the narrow sense Atlantic White-Tern; TWBF 2026 lists Taiwan's 白燕鷗 as G. candida, Blue-billed White-Tern.
日本絨螯蟹. The build gives it no name because the Catalogue of Life offers two, Japanese mitten crab and Mokuzu crab; WoRMS lists Japanese mitten crab first, and it is the name in general use.

紅耳泥龜, on the invasive register with 25 records. A subspecies shows its species' name, and this one's is Pond Slider, with Red-eared Slider not even among the alternates, so a search for the name everyone uses found nothing. Red-eared Slider is iNaturalist's name for Trachemys scripta elegans. Pond Slider stays searchable.
黃耳龜, Trachemys scripta scripta. As for the red-eared slider: iNaturalist's name for this subspecies, which the build does not ask for. Pond Slider stays searchable.

豎琴蛙, the harp frog. iNaturalist's name, Ryukyu Brown Frog, is left over from the okinavana/psaltes swap (Matsui 2007): the Ryukyu brown frog is Rana ulma. Kampira Falls Frog and Yaeyama Harpist Frog are this frog's names (AmphibiaWeb, Amphibian Species of the World), and were already its alternates. The alts column keeps Ryukyu Brown Frog from finding this frog in a search.

大口黑鱸, on the invasive register. Since the 2022 revision iNaturalist files the Florida bass under Micropterus salmoides and the largemouth bass under M. nigricans, so it names this row Florida Bass; TaiCOL's M. salmoides is the largemouth bass. The alts column drops iNaturalist's Florida bass names and keeps its names for the largemouth.
alts: Largemouth Black Bass|American Black Bass|Green Bass|Green Trout

note: 銀鷗. TaiCOL keeps the herring gull whole, with Taiwan's birds as its subspecies vegae and mongolicus; Clements v2025 split those off as Vega Gull and Mongolian Gull, which the subspecies get from the build, and calls what is left European Herring Gull, a bird Taiwan does not have. TWBF 2026 lists only the split species. Herring Gull is the name of the species as TaiCOL draws it.

布氏鯨, Bryde's whale. MDD v2.5 splits it and gives Balaenoptera edeni in the narrow sense the name Eden's Whale; TaiCOL keeps B. edeni whole, with the subspecies edeni and brydei, and 布氏鯨 is Bryde's whale. The subspecies brydei gets Bryde's Whale from the build; edeni has its own row.
布氏鯨, Balaenoptera edeni edeni, the small form, which is MDD's Eden's Whale. Without this row it would inherit Bryde's Whale from the species row above.

紅竹蛇. iNaturalist raised Taiwan's subspecies kawakamii to a species, the Taiwanese Bamboo Ratsnake, and keeps Red Mountain Ratsnake for the mainland snakes. TaiCOL keeps kawakamii as a subspecies of Oreocryptophis porphyraceus, and its 310 records already read Taiwanese Bamboo Ratsnake; this gives the species row in Taiwan the same name. Red Mountain Ratsnake stays searchable.

雲豹. MDD v2.5 calls it Mainland Clouded Leopard, after the split from the Sunda clouded leopard. As with the leopard cat, Mainland reads wrong on a Taiwanese animal; Clouded Leopard is the IUCN and CITES name. MDD's name stays searchable. The subspecies 臺灣雲豹 has its own row. Needs the team's OK, like the leopard cat default.

中華穿山甲. MDD v2.5 calls it Short-tailed Pangolin; Chinese Pangolin is the IUCN and CITES name and the English of TaiCOL's own Chinese one. MDD's name stays searchable. Taiwan's subspecies has its own row. Needs the team's OK, like the leopard cat default.

臺灣穿山甲, Manis pentadactyla pentadactyla, 27 records. Inheriting its species' name would put Chinese Pangolin beside 臺灣穿山甲. Taiwan Pangolin is iNaturalist's name for this subspecies; Formosan Pangolin, which much of the literature uses, and the species' names stay searchable. Needs the team's OK, like the leopard cat default.

臺灣雲豹, Neofelis nebulosa brachyura, Taiwan's own clouded leopard. Inheriting its species' name gave it MDD's Mainland Clouded Leopard, and then the Clouded Leopard above. Formosan Clouded Leopard is the name it goes by in English, and iNaturalist lists it among the species' names. The species' names stay searchable. Needs the team's OK, like the leopard cat default.

臺灣野兔, Lepus sinensis formosus, 71 public records. Inheriting its species' name put Chinese Hare beside 臺灣野兔, as it would have put Chinese Pangolin beside 臺灣穿山甲. Taiwan Hare is iNaturalist's name for this subspecies. Chinese Hare stays searchable. Needs the team's OK, like the leopard cat default.

家鵝, Anser anser domesticus, the farmyard goose. Inheriting its species' name called it a Graylag Goose, the wild bird, the same slip as GBIF calling a dog a gray wolf. Domestic Goose is what 家鵝 says. The wild bird's names stay searchable.

紅嘴黑鵯, 42 records. TaiCOL now ranks Taiwan's bird as its own species, Hypsipetes nigerrima; Clements v2025 and AviList keep it as H. leucocephalus nigerrimus, so no source names the species and the build left it blank. Black Bulbul is the name this bird is known by and the one the site already showed. For the team to review if a checklist gives the split species its own English name.
reviewer: claude (keeps the site's name after TaiCOL's split)

note: 灰喉山椒鳥, 4 records. TaiCOL now ranks Taiwan's bird as its own species, Pericrocotus griseogularis; Clements v2025 and AviList keep it in P. solaris, Gray-chinned Minivet, so no source names the species and the build left it blank. The name the site already showed is kept. For the team to review if a checklist gives the split species its own English name.
reviewer: claude (keeps the site's name after TaiCOL's split)
